newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower in thin range trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower in thin range trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished easier on Tuesday as Tokyo players returned from a long weekend seeing little reason to buy stocks after Wall Street's uninspired performance in the last two sessions.
Dealers said the near-term outlook was weak, but the market looked well supported around the psychological 20,000 level.
Nikkei 225 September futures ended 140 points lower at 20,175 after reaching an early high of 20,330. Volume was a light 10,190 lots.
The July MSCI index contract ended 14.0 lower at 409.9 on volume of 1,850 lots.
The pullback began in the last hour of trading and was driven by locals shorting the contract as the cash index slumped, Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary.
Activity was also depressed by traders' reluctance to take large positions ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony later in the day.
The release of Japan's indices of leading and coincident indicators had no impact on the market as the figures were within expectations, a senior dealer at an Asian house said.
He said the September Nikkei faced initial resistance around 20,300 and then at 20,500.
Taiwan stock index futures ended sharply lower in line with a sell-off on the Taipei stock market, where players took profit on electronic shares.
